title: spec: `ActionSchema.newTabUrl` is a "path template" in its JSDoc but a "URL template" in its describe; an absolute value opens backend origin + the URL
body:
## Source

Open question from the #26747 card thread (PR #26922, report comment 6454047244), checked by the ui seat on `origin/main` `5ce3404a`. Filed for the spec lane: the ui seat does not take contract-tier work.

## Problem

`packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts` (~1701-1709) says two different things about `newTabUrl`:
- The JSDoc says "A path template the renderer navigates the pre-opened tab to", naming the cloud `/sso-open` endpoint as the example.
- `.describe()` and the action form's help text (`action.form.ts` ~153) say "Direct new-tab URL template".

The console's fast path (`createConsoleServerActionHandler`, and after PR #26922 also `type: 'api'` actions) treats it as a path and prefixes the backend origin. QA's repro for #26747 used `https://example.com/export/{recordId}`, and that value opens a tab at origin + `https://example.com/…`. Nothing refuses it at authoring, so AI-written metadata can carry an absolute value silently.

## Target (the spec seat measures and chooses)

- **A (thread's recommendation):** refuse at authoring. `newTabUrl` must start with `/`, matching "path template" and the same-backend, auth-enforcing endpoint the key exists for. This is a narrowing, so it needs a contract review and a stored-metadata survey.
- **B:** declare absolute `http(s)` values legal and have the renderer navigate them verbatim. This is a widening, and it needs a renderer follow-up in `ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/consoleServerAction.ts`.

Either way, the JSDoc, `.describe()` and the form help text should say the same thing.

## Acceptance

One meaning, stated identically in all three places. An authored value outside that meaning is either refused at parse (A) or navigated as declared (B, with its ui follow-up).

Related: #26747, PR #26922.
